jobs.title: Treasury Analyst II
jobs.description:
I. Job Summary

A Treasury Analyst II plays a key role in analyzing financial assurance activities, supporting strategic decision-making, and collaborating across departments to drive efficiency. This is an opportunity to work in a fast-paced environment where your insights will contribute to decisions made on treasury and financial assurance activities

II. Essential Duties and Responsibilities
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Other minor duties may be assigned.
- Actively assess and assign the incoming financial assurance requests. This will include completing an initial assessment of the requests to determine prioritization and assign responsibility to team members. May include helping to manage contractor and or other treasury staff as needed. Perform independent reviews of financial assurance requests to evaluate and recommend correct course of action to achieve desired results.
- Collaborate and coordinate efforts between business unit management, corporate management and external surety brokers and financial institutions to ensure that instruments presented are within specifications, company policy, and negotiated and available credit lines.
- Assist in monitoring and assessing the cost of the financial assurance portfolio, which includes reviewing related invoices for accuracy, processing them for payment in accordance with company policies, working with accounting to ensure expense recognition is appropriate and preparing summary analyses of the costs.
- Use professional judgment and accounting/finance experience to assess the company’s overall financial position (computation of key financial ratios, benchmarking and stress testing), which will contribute to the compilation of financial presentations to management, the Board of Directors, senior management or the credit rating agencies as well as quarterly compliance reporting.
- Assist in preparing presentations of the current state of the company and the financial assurance program for management and external parties such as surety underwriters and credit rating agencies.
- Proactively lead projects by preparing, communicating, and carrying out a project plan that includes clear goals, a defined timeline, measurable milestones and ultimately action items or recommendations.
- Manage responsibilities and deadlines to ensure that customer (field organization) needs are met on a timely and effective basis.
- Proactively communicate in a clear, concise, and timely manner with members of internal operations management and external parties, including financial institutions, insurance and surety companies.
- Actively participate in analysis, reviews and recommendations of leases submitted by the field. For approved leases, partner with internal management and financial institutions to coordinate the negotiation and execution of capital leases.
- Assists in the daily operations of captive insurance companies and in the review of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial activity. Participate in monitoring and managing of the captive investments portfolio.
- Prepare accurate month and quarter-end reports and reconciliations to support accounting reporting requirements.
- Actively assist in process reviews and recommendations for increased efficiency in line with our continuous improvement efforts.
- Provide analytical support to the Treasury and Risk Management department on ad hoc/special projects.

III. Qualifications

A. Required Qualifications

- Bachelor's Degree (accredited) in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or similar area of study, or in lieu of degree,
- High School Diploma or GED (accredited)
- 4 years of relevant experience and
- 3 years of previous experience (in addition to education requirement).

B. Preferred Qualifications

- Self-motivated individual that works well as part of a team but is also able to be a strong individual contributor.
- Ability to work in a fast-paced environment as a member of a team responsible for managing a broad and high volume set of financial instruments.
- Strong organizational skills to plan and prioritize workflow.
- Willingness to take responsibility of assigned work areas and be held accountable for all assigned tasks.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
- Demonstrates a customer-focused approach when interacting with customers (field organization).
- Proficient with Word, Excel, Access, PowerPoint, PowerBI and Adobe.

IV. Physical Requirements

Listed below are key points regarding physical demands, physical and occupational risks, and the work environment of the job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job.

Office: This job primarily operates in a professional office environment and routinely requires the use of standard office equipment such as computers, phones, copy machines, etc.

At WM, each eligible employee receives a competitive total compensation package that includes medical, dental, vision, life insurance, and short-term disability. II.  Essential Duties and Responsibilities:   To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.  Other minor duties may be assigned.
- Coordinate with a large number of landfills to facilitate the creation of biogas tokens in support of the RNG process.      Development of process documentation will be a key responsibility.
- Support EPA registration of landfills associated with new RNG developments.
- Q/C and submit data to the EPA via EMTS and voluntary markets via M-RETS.
- Work in conjunction with peers to support the RIN splitting process via CNG/LNG dispensing stations.
- Staying current with all relevant RNG regulations and downstream markets, with a primary focus around landfills and CNG dispensing stations.
- Connect regional stakeholders and WMRE staff in discussions around potential projects related to compliance tasks.
- Pull data and reports from various operational and financial databases; providing the information in the format required by various regulatory agencies.
- Support Quality Assurance Program (QAP) activities – supply affidavits, data, and documentation to stakeholders.
- Support Low Carbon Fuel Standard (LCFS) Verification and Validation – fuel pathway data requests, quarterly fuel transactions, verifier requests.
- Update Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS), LCFS, Canadian Clean Fuel Regulations (CFR), and International Sustainability and Carbon Certification (ISCC) program registrations as necessary, i.e. changes at RNG plants, addition of new fueling stations, etc. Coordinate updates with business and compliance stakeholders.
